correctness.rationale: For unit intervals of ply <=2 nonadjacent overlaps are impossible. The realizable strict orders on a connected component are exactly matching-indexed adjacent-swap permutations; each matching is geometrically realized. An explicit recursive common supersequence has length 2m-1; induction on the occurrences of label m proves a matching lower bound, and label projection adds optimal costs across components. Direct checker exhaustively tested all 255 interval overlap masks through n=8 and exact BFS minima through n=6; finite checks are secondary to the proof.

value.rationale: Exact sharp optimum for all unit-ply-two configurations resolves a natural first nontrivial ply regime of interval-sorting preprocessing, with essential component dependence, matching-based realizable-order classification, Fibonacci count and optimal O(n log n) construction. This is more than a routine numerical improvement to the existing generic 8n upper bound; it supplies a minimum and structural combinatorial explanation, independent of smoothness claims.
